title: World Bank, Ukraine, EU and UN estimate reconstruction needs at 524 billion dollars in RDNA4
body:
On 25 February 2025 the World Bank Group, the Government of Ukraine, the European Commission and the United Nations released the fourth Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment, known as RDNA4. It estimated the cost of reconstruction and recovery over the next decade at 524 billion US dollars, or 506 billion euros, about 2.8 times Ukraine's estimated nominal GDP for 2024. The assessment covered damage from 24 February 2022 to 31 December 2024.

Direct damage was estimated at 176 billion dollars, up from 152 billion in the RDNA3 report of February 2024. The most affected sectors were housing, transport, energy, commerce and industry, and education. Long-term needs were largest in housing (about 84 billion dollars), transport (about 78 billion), energy and extractives (about 68 billion), commerce and industry (about 64 billion) and agriculture (about 55 billion), with debris clearance and management needing about 13 billion across sectors.

The report said 13 percent of the total housing stock had been damaged or destroyed, affecting more than 2.5 million households, and that damaged or destroyed energy assets had risen 70 percent since RDNA3. Regions nearest the front line sustained about 72 percent of total damage. Ukraine's government allocated 7.37 billion dollars for 2025 priorities, leaving a financing gap of 9.96 billion, and the World Bank said the private sector could potentially cover a third of total needs.
